nodes.title: Kisin's Hypothesis (1.2.6) (admissible lattice with the Henniart type inside) and its proof for abelian types, Theorem (1.2.8)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd. Following Kisin Section (1.1), a type (k, tau, psi) consists of an integer k >= 2, a representation tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(E) with open kernel that is of Galois type (it extends to the Weil group W_Qp), and a continuous character psi: G_Qp -> O^x with psi chi_cyc^{2-k}|_{I_Qp} ~ det tau; a 2-dimensional representation V of G_Qp is of type (k, tau, psi) if it is potentially semi-stable of type tau with Hodge-Tate weights 0, k-1 and determinant psi chi_cyc. Put sigma(k, tau) = sigma(tau) (x)_E Sym^{k-2} E^2, where sigma(tau) is Henniart's type (for scalar tau ~ chi + chi, sigma(tau) (x) chi^{-1} o det is the Steinberg representation of functions on P^1(F_p) with average value 0). Hypothesis (1.2.6) for (k, tau, psi): for every finite E'/E and every 2-dimensional E'-representation V of G_Qp of type (k, tau, psi) there exists an admissible O_E'-lattice Pi with central character psi (a p-adically complete and separated GL_2(Q_p)-representation on an O-module such that every Pi (x) Z/p^n is admissible of finite length, (1.2.5)) with V(Pi) (x)_{Z_p} Q_p ~ V, where V(Pi) = lim V(Pi (x) Z/p^n) is Colmez's functor (Theorem (1.2.4)), and a GL_2(Z_p)-equivariant inclusion sigma(k, tau) -> Pi (x)_{Z_p} Q_p. Theorem (1.2.8): if tau is of abelian type (tau has an abelian extension to W_Qp, which is stronger than tau having abelian image) then a Pi as in (1.2.6) exists. The published JAMS version (footnotes 1 and 3, pp. 642 and 649; absent from the 2008 DVI) adds that the revised version of Colmez's [Co 2] asserts that (1.2.6) always holds, the proof at press time relying on forthcoming work of Emerton on local-global compatibility.
hypotheses: p odd (Section (1.0): 'Throughout p will denote an odd prime').

Abelian type: tau extends to an abelian representation of W_Qp. Kisin states no equivalence with condition (2) of his main theorem. In the proof of Theorem (2.2.17) [DVI; (2.2.18) in JAMS] he passes from its condition (1) (rho|G_Fv becomes semi-stable over an abelian extension of F_v) to Corollary (2.2.16) [DVI; (2.2.17) in JAMS], whose hypothesis is (1.2.6) for each tau_v; the step 'semi-stable over an abelian extension, hence tau_v of abelian type, hence (1.2.6) by (1.2.8)' is used without comment.

The existence of Pi with V(Pi) (x) Q_p ~ V alone is attributed to [Ki 6, Thm 0.1] (Kisin's appendix to Colmez's [Co 2]) for every 2-dimensional V, except when p = 3 and the residual representation has the form (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi (2008 DVI, p. 9) -- printed (1 *; 0 omega) (x) chi in JAMS p. 649 -- or Ind_{G_{Q_{p^2}}}^{G_Qp} omega_2^2 (x) chi (remark (1.2.7)). [Ki 6] was not read.

Irreducible V: Pi is constructed in [BB 1, Section 4] (Berger-Breuil, 'Sur quelques representations potentiellement cristallines de GL2(Qp)') and [Co 1, Thm 0.4] (Colmez, 'La serie principale unitaire de GL2(Qp)', 2007 preprint), and V(Pi) (x) Q_p ~ V follows by comparing [BB 1, Thm 5.2.7] and [Co 1, Thm 0.6] with [Co 2, Prop 4.26] ([Co 2] = the earlier, shorter 2007 preprint of Colmez's (phi, Gamma)-module paper, JAMS footnote 2). None of these was read.

Reducible V: uses the lattices P-bar(chi_1, chi_2) in continuous parabolic inductions (Lemma 1.2.10), non-triviality of V on non-trivial extensions ([Co 2] Thm 5.1) and constructions of extensions by Breuil-Emerton [BE] Thm 2.2.2 and Breuil [Br 3].
proofSteps: Irreducible V of abelian type: take Pi from [BB 1, Section 4] and [Co 1, Thm 0.4]; V(Pi) (x) Q_p ~ V by comparing [BB 1, Thm 5.2.7] and [Co 1, Thm 0.6] with [Co 2, Prop 4.26] (the assignment V -> Pi in [BB 1] is contravariant, so the formulae of [BB 1, Lem 5.2.4] differ slightly from those of [Co 2, Section 4.1]). The source gives no separate argument for the inclusion sigma(k, tau) -> Pi (x) Q_p in this case; it is left to the cited constructions, which were not read.
Reducible V = extension of V(chi_2) by V(chi_1), with Hodge-Tate weights k-1 of chi_1 and 0 of chi_2: Lemma 1.2.10 gives admissible lattices P-bar(chi_1, chi_2) with V(P-bar(chi_1,chi_2)) = O(chi_1).

Applying V to an extension 0 -> P-bar(chi_1,chi_2) -> Pi -> P-bar(chi_2,chi_1) -> 0 (1.2.9) gives an extension of O(chi_2) by O(chi_1), non-trivial if (1.2.9) is ([Co 2] Thm 5.1); it suffices to build a non-trivial (1.2.9) when chi_1 chi_2^{-1} != chi_cyc (Breuil-Emerton) and a 2-dimensional space of them when chi_1 chi_2^{-1} = chi_cyc (Breuil).
acceptance: For V crystalline irreducible with Hodge-Tate weights (0, k-1) and tau = 1 + 1, check that the locally algebraic vectors of the Pi of (1.2.6) are Sym^{k-2} (x) pi with pi an unramified principal series, and that sigma(k, tau) = st (x) Sym^{k-2} E^2 (Kisin 1.1: sigma(tau) is the Steinberg type when tau is scalar), not Sym^{k-2} E^2 itself, embeds K-equivariantly.
Record that Paskunas 2015 Proposition 4.14 (with Colmez VI.6.50 and Emerton 3.3.22) supersedes (1.2.6) for rho-bar with End = k and p >= 5, so R30.6 does not depend on the abelian-type restriction.

nodes.title: Paskunas 2015, Theorem 1.1: Breuil-Mezard cycles when End(rho-bar) = k and p >= 5
nodes.statement: Let p >= 5, L/Q_p finite with ring of integers O, uniformiser varpi and residue field k, and let rho-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(k) be continuous with End_{G_Qp}(rho-bar) = k, with universal deformation ring R_rho-bar and universal deformation rho^un. A p-adic Hodge type (w, tau, psi) is: w = (a, b) integers with b > a; tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(L) with open kernel; psi: G_Qp -> O^x continuous with psi = det rho-bar (mod varpi) and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b} det tau; rho^un_n is of type (w, tau, psi) if it is potentially semi-stable with Hodge-Tate weights w, determinant psi and WD(rho^un_n)|_{I_Qp} = tau. Then (i) there is a reduced, two-dimensional, O-torsion free quotient R^psi_rho-bar(w,tau) (resp. R^{psi,cr}_rho-bar(w,tau)) of R_rho-bar such that n in m-Spec R_rho-bar[1/p] lies in m-Spec R^psi(w,tau)[1/p] (resp. R^{psi,cr}(w,tau)[1/p]) iff rho^un_n is potentially semi-stable (resp. potentially crystalline) of type (w,tau,psi); (ii) for every irreducible smooth k-representation sigma of K = GL_2(Z_p) there is a one-dimensional cycle z(sigma, rho-bar) of R_rho-bar, independent of w and tau, with z_1(R^psi(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m_sigma(w,tau) z(sigma,rho-bar) and z_1(R^{psi,cr}(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m^cr_sigma(w,tau) z(sigma,rho-bar), where m_sigma(w,tau) (resp. m^cr_sigma) is the multiplicity of sigma in the semisimplified reduction of a K-stable lattice in sigma(w,tau) = sigma(tau) (x) Sym^{b-a-1} L^2 (x) det^a (resp. sigma^cr(w,tau)), sigma(tau), sigma^cr(tau) being Henniart's types; (iii) z(sigma, rho-bar) is nonzero iff Hom_K(sigma, beta) is nonzero, beta the smooth k-representation of GL_2(Q_p) attached to rho-bar by Colmez (atome automorphe), and then its Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is 1, except when rho-bar = (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi with * peu ramifie, where it is 2. The source says the result is new only for rho-bar = (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi, the other cases being due to Kisin 2009a.
hypotheses: p >= 5: assumed in Theorem 1.1 and from Section 3 onwards ('From now on we assume that p >= 5 unless it is stated otherwise'); Sections 5 and 7 are explicitly prime-free, and Propositions 6.20 and 6.21 use p > 2.

End_{G_Qp}(rho-bar) = k, i.e. rho-bar absolutely irreducible or a non-split extension of two distinct characters (proof of Lemma 4.6). Split reducible rho-bar and non-split self-extensions (chi *; 0 chi) are NOT covered.

Determinant normalisation of this source: det = psi and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b} det tau (p. 2, checked on the page image); local class field theory sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenii and eps corresponds to x|x| (Section 3). Paskunas 2016 and Tung use det = psi*eps instead.
Case split of Section 6: generic = rho-bar irreducible or (chi_1 *; 0 chi_2) with chi_1 chi_2^{-1} not in {omega, 1}; non-generic = (chi omega *; 0 chi), treated as non-split in Theorem 6.24.

Imported, not proved in the source: from Paskunas 2013 [53] the isomorphism E-tilde = R^psi_rho-bar and hypothesis (N2) (Proposition 6.1 cites [53] Prop. 6.3, Cor. 8.7, Thm. 10.72, Cor. 10.71), the block decomposition and irreducible constituents (Lemma 4.8 cites [53] Prop. 5.36 and Cors. 6.8, 8.13-8.15, 9.35-9.37, 10.106, Prop. 10.107), V-check determining non-ordinary Pi (Lemma 4.7 cites [53] Thm. 11.4), locally algebraic vectors of principal series extensions ([53] Lem. 11.5, 12.5, 12.6); Colmez [18] VI.6.50 and Emerton [28] 3.3.22 for locally algebraic vectors in absolutely irreducible Pi(kappa(n)); Dospinescu [20] Thm. 1.4, Prop. 1.3 for (RED) in the supercuspidal case; Breuil-Paskunas [13] Cor. 9.11 (Theorem 5.2); Henniart [35] types; Breuil-Mezard [11] Thm. 5.3.1(i) and Fontaine-Laffaille theory (Proposition 6.23, Theorem 4.15).
proofSteps: Section 2 formalism (Theorem 2.42): for R complete local noetherian with residue field k and N in Mod^pro_K(O) finitely generated over R[[K]], set M(Theta) = Hom_O(Hom^cont_{O[[K]]}(N, Theta^d), O) and Pi(m) = Hom^cont_O(m^0 (x)-hat_R N, L). If (a) N is projective in Mod^pro_K(O), (b) R/ann M(Theta) is equidimensional with all associated primes minimal, (c) there is a dense Sigma in Supp M(Theta) inside m-Spec R[1/p] with dim Hom_K(V, Pi(kappa(n))) = 1 and dim Hom_K(V, Pi(R_n/n^2)) <= d, then R/a is reduced of dimension d and z_{d-1}(R/(varpi, a)) = sum_sigma m_sigma z_{d-1}(M(sigma)). Theorem 2.44 gives (a) and (b) when R is Cohen-Macaulay, N is R-flat and projdim_{O[[P]]} (k (x)-hat N) + max_sigma dim M(sigma) <= dim R.

Section 4: N in C(O) with R^psi -> End(N) satisfying (N0) k (x)-hat N of finite length and finitely generated over O[[K]], (N1) Hom_{SL_2(Q_p)}(1, N^dual) = 0, (N2) V-check(N) = rho^un as R^psi[[G_Qp]]-modules. Lemma 4.3 gives V-check(Pi(m)) = m (x) V-check(N); Proposition 4.9 describes Pi(kappa(n)); Proposition 4.14 shows dim Hom_K(sigma(w,tau), Pi(kappa(n))) <= 1 with equality iff rho^un_n is potentially semi-stable of type (w,tau,psi); Theorem 4.15 builds R^psi(w,tau) = R^psi/sqrt(ann M(Theta)).

Corollary 4.21 (from Theorem 4.19 (RED) and Lemmas 4.18, 4.20) bounds dim Hom_K(V, Pi(R^psi_n/n^2)) <= 2 for almost all n in Supp M(Theta), outside the case rho-bar = (delta-bar omega *; 0 delta-bar), b - a = 1, tau = chi + chi.

Generic case (Section 6.1): N = P-tilde, a projective envelope of pi^dual in C(O). Proposition 6.1 (from [53]) gives (N0)-(N2) and E-tilde = R^psi; Theorem 5.2 gives x in E-tilde with P-tilde/xP-tilde a projective envelope of (soc_K pi)^dual in Mod^pro_{K,zeta}(O), so P-tilde is projective over K (Corollary 5.3); Corollary 6.4 gives M(Theta) Cohen-Macaulay of dimension 2; Theorem 6.6 applies Theorem 2.42 and computes M(sigma) = R/a with R/a = k[[x]] when sigma lies in the multiplicity-free soc_K pi (Remark 6.2).

Non-generic case (Section 6.2, twist to rho-bar = (omega *; 0 1), zeta trivial mod varpi): Colmez's beta with socle Sp and semisimplification Sp + 1 + pi_alpha (Lemma 6.7); Theorem 6.10 identifies the deformation functor of beta^dual in C(O) with that of rho-bar with determinant eps*zeta, R_beta = R^psi = O[[x1,x2,x3]]; with N the universal deformation of beta^dual, Lemma 6.13 gives (N0)-(N2), Propositions 6.20 and 6.21 give max dim M(sigma) <= 1 and projdim beta^dual = 3, so Corollary 6.22 verifies Theorem 2.44; Proposition 6.23 handles w = (a, a+1), tau = chi + chi using Breuil-Mezard's multiplicity computation and Fontaine-Laffaille theory; Theorem 6.24 is the cycle identity for non-split rho-bar.
Theorem 1.1 is the combination of Theorems 6.6 and 6.24 with z(sigma, rho-bar) := z_1(M(sigma)).
acceptance: For each of the three admissible shapes of rho-bar (absolutely irreducible; generic non-split reducible; (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi tres ramifie or peu ramifie) check that the set of sigma with z(sigma, rho-bar) nonzero equals the K-socle constituents listed in Remark 6.2 and Theorem 6.24 (st (x) det^m, plus det^m only in the peu ramifie case).
Check that no application uses this theorem for split rho-bar (Hu-Tan node) or for a non-split self-extension (chi *; 0 chi), whose endomorphism ring is 2-dimensional.
Check the determinant convention (det = psi, psi|_I = eps^{a+b} det tau) against Paskunas 2016 / Tung (det = psi*eps) before combining cycles from different sources.

nodes.title: Hu-Tan 2015, Theorem 1.3: Breuil-Mezard cycles for rho-bar = chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 != chi_2, p >= 5
nodes.statement: Fix p >= 5 and E/Q_p sufficiently large (O, varpi, residue field F). Let rho-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(F) be continuous and isomorphic to chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 != chi_2, and R^box(rho-bar) its universal framed deformation ring. A p-adic Hodge type (k, tau, psi) is an integer k >= 2, tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(E) with open kernel, and psi: G_Qp -> O^x continuous with psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{k-2} det tau; rho: G_Qp -> GL_2(E) is of type (k, tau, psi) if it is potentially semi-stable with Hodge-Tate weights (0, k-1), WD(rho)|_{I_Qp} = tau and det rho = psi eps. Let R^{box,psi}(k,tau,rho-bar) and R^{box,psi}_cr(k,tau,rho-bar) be Kisin's potentially semi-stable and potentially crystalline quotients (Theorem 1.1: p-torsion free, reduced with smooth 4-dimensional components after inverting p). Then there are 4-dimensional cycles Z_{n,m} of R^box(rho-bar), independent of (k, tau, psi), such that Z(R^{box,psi}(k,tau,rho-bar)/varpi) = sum_{n,m} a_{n,m}(k,tau) Z_{n,m} and Z(R^{box,psi}_cr(k,tau,rho-bar)/varpi) = sum_{n,m} a^cr_{n,m}(k,tau) Z_{n,m}, with Z_{n,m} = Z(R^{box,psi}_cr(n+2, (omega-tilde^m)^{+2}, rho-bar)/varpi); here a_{n,m}(k,tau) is the multiplicity of sigma_{n,m} = Sym^n F^2 (x) det^m (0 <= n <= p-1, 0 <= m <= p-2) in the semisimplified reduction of sigma(k,tau) = Sym^{k-2} E^2 (x) sigma(tau). nodes.title: Tung 2021a, Theorem 1.2: Breuil-Mezard cycles for every residual type when p is odd, proved by patching
nodes.statement: Assume p > 2. Let E/Q_p be sufficiently large (O, varpi, k), r-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(k) any continuous representation, R^box_r-bar its universal framed deformation ring and R^{box,psi}_r-bar the quotient with determinant psi eps. A p-adic Hodge type (lambda, tau, psi) is lambda = (a, b) integers with a > b, tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(E) with open kernel and psi: G_Qp -> O^x continuous with psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b-1} det tau; r is of type (lambda, tau, psi) if potentially semi-stable with Hodge-Tate weights (a, b), WD(r|_{I_Qp}) = tau and det r = psi eps; R^{box,psi}_r-bar(lambda,tau) and R^{box,psi,cr}_r-bar(lambda,tau) are Kisin's reduced, 4-dimensional (if nonzero), p-torsion free quotients. Then for each irreducible smooth k-representation sigma-bar of K there is a 4-dimensional cycle C_sigma-bar(r-bar) of R^{box,psi}_r-bar, independent of lambda and tau, with Z(R^{box,psi}_r-bar(lambda,tau)/varpi) = sum m_sigma-bar(lambda,tau) C_sigma-bar(r-bar) and Z(R^{box,psi,cr}_r-bar(lambda,tau)/varpi) = sum m^cr_sigma-bar(lambda,tau) C_sigma-bar(r-bar), where m_sigma-bar is the multiplicity of sigma-bar in the semisimplified reduction of sigma(lambda,tau) = Sym^{a-b-1} E^2 (x) det^b (x) sigma(tau). The source says this is new for p = 3 and r-bar a twist of an extension of the trivial character by the mod p cyclotomic character. Corollary 4.6: every irreducible component of R^box_r-bar(sigma)[1/p] is automorphic, i.e. lies in the support of the patched module M_infty(sigma) (Definition 3.2: that support is a union of irreducible components of Spec R^box_r-bar(sigma), called the automorphic components).
hypotheses: p > 2 (Theorem 1.2; Section 3 onwards 'From now on we make the assumption p > 2').
Normalisation (page image p. 3): lambda = (a, b) with a > b, psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b-1} det tau, det r = psi eps.

The proof is GLOBAL, not local: it uses a suitable globalisation of r-bar over an imaginary CM field (Emerton-Gee [EG14] Cor. A.7), the patched module M_infty of [CEG+16] for definite unitary groups with its arithmetic action (AA1)-(AA4), local-global compatibility ([CEG+16] Thm. 4.35, [Pyv18] Thm. 6.1), the faithfulness and density results of Emerton-Paskunas [EP20] (Thms. 5.1, 5.3, 6.3), Wang-Erickson's Cayley-Hamilton finiteness [WE18] Prop. 3.6, the capture family of Paskunas 2016 Prop. 2.7, Allen [All16] Thm. 1.2.7, Barnet-Lamb-Gee-Geraghty [BLGG13] Thm. A.4.1 for ordinary components, and Colmez-Dospinescu-Paskunas [CDP14] Cor. 1.7, Thm. 1.3, Thm. 3.14. Further imports in the proof: Colmez [Col10] Thm VI.6.50 (Theorem 4.1); Paskunas 2013 Lemma 10.26 and Prop 2.8/[CDP14] Thm 3.14(i) (Corollary 4.3); Paskunas 2013 Cor B.5 and Boeckle [Boc10] Thms 4.2, 5.2 (irreducibility of Spec R^box, Proposition 3.9); Emerton-Gee [EG14] Lemma 5.5.1 (proof of Theorem 1.2), Thm 5.5.2 (Corollary 4.6) and Prop 3.3.1 (Remark 4.5); Paskunas 2015 Lemma 2.3 and Cor 2.5 (projectivity, AA3); Nekovar [Nek93] Prop 1.24 (Proposition 4.4); Boston-Lenstra-Ribet [BLR91] Thm 1 (Theorem 4.1).

Exceptional component: for r-bar ~ (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi, lambda = (a+1, a), tau = eta + eta, Proposition 4.4 does not show the semi-stable non-crystalline component automorphic; the cycle identity is then checked directly from Breuil-Mezard [BM02] Thm. 5.3.1 and [KW09] Section 3.2.7.

For p = 3 and the block B = {1, Sp, omega o det, Sp (x) omega o det} (x) delta o det, the source proves its own Ext computations (Section 2.3, Lemmas 2.2-2.6) to extend Paskunas 2013's equivalence V-check: D(O)[B] -> Mod^pro_{G_Qp}(O)[B] (Proposition 2.8).
proofSteps: Section 2.3-2.4: for p = 3 and B = {1, Sp, omega o det, Sp (x) omega o det}, compute e(pi', pi) (from Paskunas 2010b Thm. 11.4), the representation tau with 0 -> Sp -> tau -> 1 + 1 -> 0 (Lemma 2.2, via Emerton's ordinary parts), Ext^1_{D(k)} between T_1, T_omega all 2-dimensional (Lemma 2.5), V-check injective on these Ext^1 (Lemma 2.6, using Colmez Props. VII.4.12, 4.24, 4.25 valid for p = 3), hence Lemma 2.7 and Proposition 2.8 (equivalence of categories) and Proposition 2.9 (V-check(pi^dual) finitely generated over k[[G_Qp]] for admissible pi).

Section 3: the fixed-central-character patched module M^psi_infty lies in C(O); V-check(M^psi_infty) is finitely generated over R^psi_infty[[G_Qp]] (Proposition 3.5), the action factors through the Cayley-Hamilton quotient (Theorem 3.7), so V-check(M^psi_infty) is finitely generated over R^psi_infty (Corollary 3.8) and faithful (Proposition 3.9); hence V-check(Pi_y) and Pi_y are nonzero for every y (Corollary 3.10).

Section 4: for r_x absolutely irreducible, V-check(Pi_y) = r_x^{+n_y} with n_y >= 1 (Theorem 4.1), so M_infty(sigma)[1/p] is supported on every non-ordinary component; Lemma 4.2 and Corollary 4.3 (n_y = 1 on an open dense set); Proposition 4.4 handles reducible (ordinary) components through [BLGG13], except the exceptional semi-stable non-crystalline component.

Proof of Theorem 1.2: define C_sigma-bar(r-bar) := Z_4(R^box_r-bar(sigma-tilde)/varpi) for the crystalline lift sigma-tilde of Remark 1.3 and compare cycles of R_infty(sigma)/varpi and M_infty(sigma)/varpi using projectivity of M_infty (Paskunas 2015 Lemma 2.3) and [EG14] Lemma 5.5.1; treat the exceptional case by direct Hilbert-Samuel computation (Remark 4.5).
Corollary 4.6 follows from Theorem 1.2 and [EG14] Thm. 5.5.2.

nodes.title: Paskunas 2016, Theorems 2.34 and 2.37: Breuil-Mezard cycles for generic residual types, no restriction on p
nodes.statement: No restriction on p. Let rho-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(k) be either absolutely irreducible (pi supersingular with V(pi) = rho-bar) or a non-split extension (chi_1 *; 0 chi_2) with chi_1 chi_2^{-1} != 1, omega^{+-1} (pi = (Ind_B^G chi_1 (x) chi_2 omega^{-1})_sm), and let R^psi be the quotient of its universal deformation ring parametrising deformations with determinant psi eps. For a p-adic Hodge type (w, tau, psi) with w = (a, b), b > a, tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(L) with open kernel, psi eps = det rho-bar (mod varpi) and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b-1} det tau: (Theorem 2.34) there is a finite set {C_sigma} of 1-dimensional cycles of R^psi/varpi, indexed by the irreducible smooth k-representations sigma of K, with z_1(R^psi(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m_sigma(w,tau) C_sigma and z_1(R^{psi,cr}(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m^cr_sigma(w,tau) C_sigma; C_sigma is nonzero iff Hom_K(sigma, pi) != 0, and then its Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is 1. (Theorem 2.37) For rho-bar = chi_1 + chi_2 with the same generic condition and framed ring R^box, there are 4-dimensional cycles C_{1,sigma}, C_{2,sigma} of R^{psi,box}/varpi with z_4(R^{psi,box}(w,tau)/varpi) = sum m_sigma(w,tau)(C_{1,sigma} + C_{2,sigma}) and the crystalline analogue; C_{1,sigma} != 0 iff Hom_K(sigma, (Ind_B^G chi_1 (x) chi_2 omega^{-1})_sm) != 0, C_{2,sigma} != 0 iff Hom_K(sigma, (Ind_B^G chi_2 (x) chi_1 omega^{-1})_sm) != 0, with multiplicity 1. (Corollary 2.38) If p = 2, psi is unramified and rho-bar is absolutely irreducible or rho-bar^ss = chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 != chi_2, then for w = (0,1), tau = 1 + 1 the framed potentially semi-stable and potentially crystalline rings coincide: every semi-stable lift with Hodge-Tate weights (0,1) is crystalline.
hypotheses: Section 2C places no restriction on p, but rho-bar must be absolutely irreducible or have rho-bar^ss = chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 chi_2^{-1} != 1, omega^{+-1}; for p = 2 (omega = 1) this excludes exactly the residual representations with scalar semisimplification, i.e. (chi *; 0 chi) and chi + chi.

Normalisation: det = psi eps and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b-1} det tau (p. 1325, checked on the page image). The sentence on p. 1326 'the determinant is equal to psi' conflicts with this and with the definition of R^psi (determinant psi eps, Section 2B1); it is read here as a typo for psi eps.
For p = 2 Henniart's types sigma(tau), sigma^cr(tau) need not be unique and a choice is made; the semisimplified reductions do not depend on the choice (p. 1326).
Key local input: V-check induces E = R^psi for the projective envelope P of pi^dual (Theorem 2.22), proved here for all p.

VII.5.2, Thm. VI.6.50, Prop. VII.4.13(iii); Berger-Breuil 2010 Cor. 5.3.4; Breuil-Emerton 2010 Prop. 2.2.1; Emerton 2010b (ordinary parts) Props. 4.2.14, 4.3.15 and Emerton-Paskunas 2010 Cor. 3.12; Paskunas 2015b Sections 2, 4, 5 (Cor. 2.5, Prop. 2.22, 2.24, 2.30, 2.32, Lemma 2.33, Thm. 5.2, Cor. 5.3, Thm. 4.19); Dospinescu 2015 for supercuspidal types (stated for p >= 5; the needed inputs det V-check(Pi) = psi eps and dim Ext^1 = 3 are Corollaries 2.24, 2.26); Emerton 2011 Section 7.4 as a global input when tau extends to an irreducible representation of W_Qp; Paskunas 2015a (On 2-adic deformations) Thm. 7.3, Rem. 7.4 for Theorem 2.37; Boeckle 2010 (p = 3) and Chenevier 2009 Prop. 4.1 (p = 2) for reducedness of R^psi.
proofSteps: Proposition 2.14: V-check induces surjections R -> E -> R^psi; the first from injectivity of Ext^1_{C(O)}(Q,Q) -> Ext^1_{G_Qp}(rho-bar, rho-bar) (Colmez Thm. VII.5.2), the second because R^psi is reduced and O-torsion free (formally smooth for p >= 5, Boeckle for p = 3, Chenevier for p = 2) and every closed point of Spec R^psi[1/p] comes from a Banach representation (Colmez-Dospinescu-Paskunas 2015 Thm. 10.1).

Propositions 2.17-2.19 and Corollary 2.20: for V = tau' (x) Sym^a L^2 (x) eta o det with tau' a type for a principal series (not special series) Bernstein component, dim Hom_K(V, Pi(kappa(n))) <= 1 and dim Hom_K(V, Pi(E_n/n^2)) <= 2, E/ann M(Theta) is reduced and O-torsion free, and E/a = R^psi/phi(a).

Theorem 2.22: the family of such V captures every projective object of Mod^pro_{K,psi}(O) (Proposition 2.7), so the annihilators intersect to zero (Lemma 2.21) and phi: E -> R^psi is injective, hence an isomorphism; V-check(P) is the universal deformation with determinant psi eps.

Section 2C: Proposition 2.27 verifies Paskunas 2015's axioms (N0)-(N2); Proposition 2.28 gives M(Theta) Cohen-Macaulay of dimension 2 and z_1(M(Theta)/varpi) = sum m_sigma z_1(M(sigma)) with M(sigma) = k[[x]] or 0; Proposition 2.30 identifies the support of M(Theta) with the potentially semi-stable (crystalline) points of type (w,tau,psi) with generic rank 1; Corollaries 2.31, 2.32 and Proposition 2.33 (reducedness via (RED), Dospinescu 2015 in the supercuspidal case) give Theorem 2.34.

Theorem 2.37 follows from Theorem 2.34 and Paskunas 2015a Thm. 7.3 and Rem. 7.4; Corollary 2.38 follows from Theorem 2.34 since for p = 2 the only irreducible k-representations of K are 1 and st, soc_K pi = 1 + st, sigma(w,tau)/varpi = st and sigma^cr(w,tau)/varpi = 1.

nodes.title: Tung 2021b, Corollary 8.0.2: Breuil-Mezard for every residual type when p = 2, proved by patching
nodes.statement: Let p = 2. (Theorem 8.0.1) Suppose p splits completely in the totally real field F (F_v ~ Q_2 for v | p), and let M_infty be the module patched in Section 4 from definite quaternion algebras over F for a suitable globalisation (Definition 4.3.2). Then for each locally algebraic type sigma the support of M_infty(sigma°) (x)_{Z_p} Q_p meets every irreducible component of R_infty(sigma)[1/p]. (Corollary 8.0.2) Let r-bar: G_Q2 -> GL_2(k) any continuous representation. For a Hodge type lambda, an inertial type tau and a continuous zeta: G_Qp -> O^x with zeta|_{I_Qp} = (Art^{-1}_{Q_p})^{lambda_1 + lambda_2} det tau, let sigma = sigma(lambda,tau) or sigma^cr(lambda,tau) be the locally algebraic type and R^zeta_r-bar(sigma) the local universal lifting ring of type sigma and determinant zeta eps. Then Conjecture 5.1.2 holds: there are non-negative integers mu_a(r-bar), indexed by Serre weights a, with e(R^zeta_r-bar(sigma)/varpi) = sum_a m_a(sigma) mu_a(r-bar) for every locally algebraic type sigma, m_a(sigma) the Jordan-Hoelder multiplicity of sigma_a in the reduction of sigma; and Conjecture 5.1.3 holds: there are 4-dimensional cycles C_a(r-bar) of R^zeta_r-bar, independent of lambda and tau, with Z(R^zeta_r-bar(sigma)/varpi) = sum_a m_a(sigma) C_a(r-bar). The source says this is new for r-bar ~ (chi *; 0 chi), chi: G_Qp -> k^x continuous.

Both conjectures are independent of the choice of zeta (Remark 5.1.4).

The proof is GLOBAL: Corollary 8.0.2 is deduced from Theorem 8.0.1 (the support of the patched quaternionic module M_infty(sigma) meets every irreducible component of R_infty(sigma)[1/p] when p splits completely in F) through the equivalences of Theorem 5.3.3 and the existence of a suitable globalisation (Lemma 4.3.3, which cites Calegari 2012 Prop. 3.2, Snowden 2009 Prop. 8.2.1 and the proof of Khare-Wintenberger II Thm. 6.1).

Theorem 8.0.1 uses Theorem 6.3.7 (V-check(Pi_y) = r_x^{+n_y} for absolutely irreducible r_x) on non-ordinary components and Theorem 7.3.1 (automorphic ordinary lifts from an ordinary R = T theorem, a variant of Thorne 2012 Thm. 10.2) on ordinary components.

The p = 2 block {1, Sp} (x) chi o det needs the source's own Ext computations and equivalence of categories (Section 1.2, Lemmas 1.2.3-1.2.7, Proposition 1.3.2), which were located but not read line by line.

Section 7: partial Hida families and ordinary patching (Corollaries 7.2.2, 7.2.3) give automorphic lifts on ordinary components (Theorem 7.3.1).
Theorem 8.0.1 combines Sections 6 and 7 place by place; Corollary 8.0.2 then follows from Theorem 5.3.3 and Lemma 4.3.3.

nodes.title: Hypothesis table: the residually modular lifting theorems behind Dieulefait-Pacetti Theorems 1.4 and 1.5
nodes.statement: Exact hypotheses of the theorems cited by Dieulefait-Pacetti, as the cited sources state them. (K) Kisin 2009a, main theorem: p > 2, rho: G_{Q,S} -> GL_2(O) continuous with (1) rho|G_Qp potentially semi-stable with distinct Hodge-Tate weights, (2) rho becomes semi-stable over an abelian extension of Q_p, (3) rho-bar odd and rho-bar|Q(zeta_p) absolutely irreducible, (4) rho-bar|G_Qp not ~ (omega chi *; 0 chi); conclusion: rho modular up to twist. Theorem 1.5 (p = 2; rho odd, finitely ramified, de Rham at 2 with Hodge-Tate weights {0, k-1}, k > 1, rho-bar modular with non-solvable image => rho matches a weight k modular form) is justified by Kisin 2009b Theorem 0.1 (k = 2, rho potentially Barsotti-Tate), Paskunas 2016 Theorem 1.1 and Tung 2021b Theorem A. This case division sits in the proofs of Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 in Section 1.2.1, not in the introduction; matched against the sources, 'the other hypothesis' is Kisin's residual condition (4) rho-bar|G_Qp not ~ (omega chi *; 0 chi), and the removal of Kisin's condition (2) goes through Hypothesis (1.2.6). review.notes: All eight nodes and eight links were checked against public copies. Four sources (Dieulefait-Pacetti, Paskunas 2015, Tung 2021a, Tung 2021b) are the exact arXiv files the drafter read (SHA-256 identical). Hu-Tan and Paskunas 2016 were read in arXiv v2 (same numbering as the published versions the packet cites; arXiv pages recorded). Kisin was read both in the public 2008 DVI (identical SHA-256 to the library copy) and in the free JAMS PDF. Main findings: (1) Kisin's residually modular theorem is 2.2.17 in the DVI but 2.2.18 in JAMS, which is the number Hu-Tan and Tung cite, and the table listed only one of its three hypotheses; (2) the Kisin node lacked the definition of the type and contained unsourced glosses; the JAMS footnotes on the general validity of (1.2.6) were missing; (3) the Dieulefait-Pacetti use map misplaced the p = 3 use of Theorem 1.4 (it is in Lemma 2.3, not Paso 6); (4) Tung 2021b's link consumes Theorem 8.0.1, not Corollary 8.0.2; (5) a missing link Paskunas 2015 -> Hu-Tan (Thm 4.2, Rem 5.7) was added; (6) five gaps added for unread imports and for shared intermediate results that have no supplier node. Source-record recommendations: add the public DVI and JAMS URLs to the Kisin source; record arXiv v2 alongside the published editions for Hu-Tan and Paskunas 2016. Status stays partial; implementationStatus stays unchecked.

checked.note: Checked against the public 2008 DVI on Kisin's homepage (SHA-256 identical to the library copy; text extracted with a reviewer-written DVI parser) and against the free JAMS PDF. Hypothesis (1.2.6), Remark (1.2.7), Theorem (1.2.8) with proof and Lemma (1.2.10) read in both. The definition of 'type (k, tau, psi)' (Kisin 1.1: tau of Galois type, HT weights 0,k-1, det = psi*chi_cyc) was missing. The 'equivalently ... condition (2)' gloss is not in the source; Kisin uses the implication only implicitly in the proof of Theorem (2.2.17) [DVI] = (2.2.18) [JAMS]. The proof step's 'crystabelline up to twist' and 'built from locally algebraic principal series' are not in the source. Remark (1.2.7) prints (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi in the DVI but (1 *; 0 omega) (x) chi in JAMS (page image p. 649 checked). JAMS footnotes 1 and 3 (absent from the DVI) say the revised [Co 2] asserts (1.2.6) always holds, with the proof relying on Emerton's local-global compatibility; this is the route by which Dieulefait-Pacetti credit Emerton 2011. Acceptance item 1 wrongly suggested sigma(k,1) = Sym^{k-2}: for scalar tau Kisin's sigma(tau) is the Steinberg type.
